risks.risk: Item mismatch: seller text says “white sand”, but photos show IBC tanks; buyer may be paying for the wrong thing.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo clearly showing the actual “white sand” (bagged or in a pile) and/or a photo of the exact item being sold with a label/quantity.
risks.if_unproven: Price as IBC tanks only (not sand), and treat condition/contents as unknown.

risks.risk: IBC tank condition: possible leaks, damaged valve/port, cracked plastic, or missing parts (tap/valve, cap). Photos don’t confirm integrity.
risks.proof: Request a short video showing the valve/port area, underside, and a close-up of any damage; include a fill/pressure test claim if available.
risks.if_unproven: Price at worst case: assume it may need repair and/or is not guaranteed leak-free.

risks.risk: Capacity/size uncertainty: “1000 litres” is not readable from the photo; could be different IBC class.
risks.proof: Request a photo of the tank’s capacity marking/label (e.g., 1000L) and the serial/ID plate.
risks.if_unproven: Price as the common 1000L class only if confirmed; otherwise price as generic IBC tank with uncertain capacity.

risks.risk: Quantity uncertainty: photo shows multiple tanks, but seller may be selling one or several.
risks.proof: Ask for the exact number of tanks included and a photo counting them.
risks.if_unproven: Price per unit at worst-case quantity (assume 1 unit).

proof_requests: Confirm what is actually for sale: IBC tanks or white sand (send clear photos of the sand if that’s what you’re buying).
Send a close-up photo of the IBC label/ID plate showing capacity (e.g., 1000L) and any chemical/previous contents info.
Send close-ups and a short video of the valve/port and bottom frame to check for leaks/damage.
State exact quantity included (how many IBC tanks) and whether they are sold individually or as a set.
